# Review pack: review-software-lifecycle

Everything a worker needs for this skill, in one file: `SKILL.md`, `references/checklist.md`, the skill's other reference files and its language-neutral standards. Language-specific standards and signals are in `packs/review-software-lifecycle.<language>.md`. Citation columns (anchors, pages, source names) are left out: cite an element by its ID in `Finding.element` and the report script fills in `standard` and `url`. `sources.md` is maintainer material and is not included.

## File: `SKILL.md`

### Review: Software Lifecycle

Assesses how the project builds, protects, versions and releases its software, as visible in repository files:
CI pipelines, release workflows, version fields, settings-as-code, CODEOWNERS, `SECURITY.md`, SAST config and
committed binaries. It uses local, pinned summaries of SemVer 2.0.0, NIST SP 800-218 SSDF 1.1, SLSA v1.2 and the
OpenSSF Scorecard checks. Git history, tags, releases and forge settings are not read.

#### Inputs

CI/CD definitions (`.github/workflows/*`, `azure-pipelines*.yml`, `.gitlab-ci.yml`, `Jenkinsfile`), release-tool
config, Dockerfiles and scripts used by CI, version-bearing manifests, settings-as-code and CODEOWNERS,
`SECURITY.md`, SAST config, and `CHANGELOG*` (version history only), per `compliance-inventory`.

#### Standards (local, authoritative)

- `references/standards/semver.md` — SV-01…SV-11. Always load.
- `references/standards/nist-ssdf.md` — SSDF-01…SSDF-19. Always load.
- `references/standards/slsa.md` — SLSA-01…SLSA-14. Always load.
- `references/standards/openssf-scorecard.md` — OSC-01…OSC-21. Always load.
- `references/standards/azure-waf-safe-deployment.md` — SDP-01 (staged rollouts). Always load.
- Do **not** fetch any URL for this skill. Do not load `references/standards/MAINTENANCE.md`.
- If no element covers a situation: apply the closest element if it clearly fits; otherwise mark the check N/A
  ("not covered by localized standard") and add `localized-standard-gap: <description>` to `notes`.

#### Procedure

1. Load `references/checklist.md`, `references/sources.md`, `references/lifecycle-signals.md` and the five
   standards files.
2. Files only: judge only what the files show. Never read Git history, tags or releases, and never assume forge
   settings. Release assets and registries are judged through the workflow steps that produce them.
3. Platform: identify the CI platform(s) and forge from `lifecycle-signals.md` §1. Apply Scorecard elements through
   the platform equivalents there; skip an element with "no equivalent on <platform>" if none exists.
4. Publish scope: decide whether the repo publishes versioned artifacts (publishable manifest with name and version,
   release or deploy pipeline, or versioned API). If not, SL-02 and SL-05 are N/A ("repo publishes no versioned
   artifacts") and SL-03 judges only SV-01, SV-07 and SV-08 on any declared version.
5. Settings (SL-04): judge SSDF-11, SSDF-15, SLSA-10…14, OSC-01…03 and OSC-05 only from settings-as-code
   (`lifecycle-signals.md` §3); otherwise skip them ("repository settings not visible in files"). Documentation
   claims are not evidence. SSDF-10 and OSC-04 (CODEOWNERS) apply whenever the forge supports CODEOWNERS. If every
   SL-04 element is skipped, SL-04 is N/A with that reason, never a failure.
6. Versions (SL-03): judge the published version field per `lifecycle-signals.md` §9 (ecosystem equivalents
   accepted; 4-part assembly/file versions are not judged; a `v` prefix only in tag patterns).
7. Committed binaries (SL-12): match `lifecycle-signals.md` §10 patterns; exclude paths matched by `.gitignore` (read as a plain file; never run Git), build-output
   and environment folders, and binaries referenced by a manifest (review-dependency-management DEP-08). Use
   confidence `medium` unless the binary sits in a source folder.
8. Boundaries: don't fail for tests in CI (review-testing TST-06), dependency pinning, lock files, SBOM or update
   automation (review-dependency-management), contributing/branching docs or change logs (review-maintainability),
   pipeline secrets or OIDC credentials (review-security-operational SMG-12), or lint/format rules
   (review-software-quality). Staged rollouts and rollback paths are judged here (SDP-01 under SL-02): fail SDP-01
   only when a production deployment job or deployment config in scope releases straight to all of production with
   no staged step (ring, canary, slot swap, blue-green), no gate between stages and no rollback step; confidence
   `medium`. Runtime redundancy and restart behaviour stay with review-reliability.
9. For each check (SL-01…SL-05, SL-07, SL-09…SL-12), evaluate only the elements it lists whose "Applies when"
   condition holds. If none apply, mark the check N/A with that reason. SL-06 and SL-08 are retired: don't evaluate
   them or write them to `checkResults`.
10. Evidence rule: fail only on concrete evidence in the files (see `lifecycle-signals.md` fail signals). Use
    confidence `medium` unless the evidence is unambiguous.
11. Severity: every Finding takes the check's default severity from `checklist.md`;
    `checkResults.severityIfFailed` is always that default.
12. Citations: set `element` to the failed element's ID (e.g. `SSDF-02`); the report script derives `standard` and
    `url` from it, so don't write them. Never cite `lifecycle-signals.md`.

#### Output

Findings, strengths and check results per `compliance-review-core`'s `finding-schema.md`.

## File: `references/lifecycle-signals.md`

### Lifecycle signals — lookup table

Local lookup table, not a standard. Use it to classify CI/CD, settings and version evidence for SL-01 … SL-12; cite
the SV/SSDF/SLSA/OSC elements, never this file. If a platform, tool or setting isn't listed and you can't classify
it, add `localized-standard-gap: unrecognized <kind> <name>` to `notes`.

#### 1. Platform and forge detection (all checks)

- GitHub: `.github/workflows/*.yml`, `.github/` folder.
- Azure DevOps: `azure-pipelines*.yml`, `.azuredevops/`.
- GitLab: `.gitlab-ci.yml`, `.gitlab/`.
- Jenkins: `Jenkinsfile`.
- Others: `.circleci/config.yml`, `bitbucket-pipelines.yml`.
- CODEOWNERS is supported on GitHub and GitLab. Azure DevOps uses a required-reviewer *policy* (settings-as-code
  only).

#### 2. Pre-merge CI triggers — OSC-06, SSDF-01, SLSA-02, SLSA-09 (SL-01)

- Pass: GitHub `on: pull_request` (or `merge_group`). GitLab `rules: if: $CI_PIPELINE_SOURCE == "merge_request_event"`
  or MR pipelines. Azure Pipelines `pr:` trigger (GitHub/Bitbucket repos) or a build-validation policy in
  settings-as-code. Jenkins multibranch with PR discovery.
- Fail: only `push`, `schedule` or `workflow_dispatch` triggers. No pipeline definition in the repository.
- Skip, don't fail: Azure Repos ignore a `pr:` block; without settings-as-code a pre-merge build isn't visible.

#### 3. Settings-as-code — SSDF-11, SSDF-15, SLSA-10 … SLSA-14, OSC-01 … OSC-03, OSC-05 (SL-04)

- Recognized forms: Terraform `github_branch_protection`, `github_repository_ruleset` (`required_pull_request_reviews`,
  `required_status_checks`, `allows_force_pushes = false`, `allows_deletions = false`, `require_code_owner_reviews`,
  `required_signatures`, tag rules); `azuredevops_branch_policy_min_reviewers`, `azuredevops_branch_policy_build_validation`;
  `gitlab_branch_protection`, `gitlab_tag_protection`; Probot `.github/settings.yml` `branches:`; exported ruleset
  JSON.
- Fail: `allows_force_pushes = true`, `required_approving_review_count = 0`, no status checks, `enforce_admins = false`
  (OSC-02).
- None of these present: skip the setting elements ("repository settings not visible in files"). Docs claims are
  not evidence.

#### 4. CODEOWNERS — OSC-04, SSDF-10 (SL-04)

- Pass: `CODEOWNERS` in the root, `.github/` or `docs/` (GitHub), or `.gitlab/` (GitLab), with a `*` rule or rules
  covering pipeline and build files.
- Fail: missing on a GitHub or GitLab repo; a file with no rule covering `.github/workflows/` (or the CI files).

#### 5. Workflow injection — OSC-07, OSC-08 (SL-09)

- Pass: untrusted values passed via `env:` and quoted as `"$VAR"`.
- Fail (GitHub): `pull_request_target`/`workflow_run` + `actions/checkout` with
  `ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}` (or `.head.ref`); `${{ github.event.issue.title }}`/`.body`,
  `pull_request.title`/`.body`, `comment.body`, `review.body`, `head_ref`, `head_commit.message`, `pages.*.page_name`
  inside `run:`.
- Fail (Azure Pipelines): `$(System.PullRequest.SourceBranch)` or `$(Build.SourceVersionMessage)` macros inside
  `script:`.
- Fail (GitLab): `$CI_MERGE_REQUEST_TITLE`/`$CI_COMMIT_MESSAGE` used unquoted in `script:`.

#### 6. Token scopes and pinning — OSC-09 … OSC-13, SSDF-05, SLSA-08 (SL-10)

- Pass (GitHub): top-level `permissions: {}` or `contents: read`, job-level writes; `uses: owner/repo@<40-hex SHA>`
  (a version comment is allowed).
- Pass (Azure Pipelines): `persistCredentials: false`; template `resources.repositories` with `ref:` to a commit.
- Pass (GitLab): `include:` with `ref:` SHA; CI job token allowlist.
- Pass (all): images `@sha256:<digest>`; installs with `npm ci`, `pip install --require-hashes`,
  `dotnet restore --locked-mode`, `poetry install --no-update`.
- Fail: no `permissions:` (inherits the repo default), `permissions: write-all`, `contents: write` at the top level;
  `uses: …@v3`/`@main`; `FROM image:tag` without digest; `curl … | sh`, `wget … | bash`, `iex (iwr …)`;
  `npm install`/`pip install pkg` without pins in CI.
- Jenkins has no token-permission scopes: skip OSC-09/OSC-10 ("no equivalent on Jenkins").
- Secret storage, OIDC and long-lived credentials are not judged here (review-security-operational SMG-12).

#### 7. Release, packaging and environments — SSDF-09, SSDF-13, SLSA-01, OSC-20 (SL-02)

- Pass: release workflow on `release:`/tag push (`v*`); registry push (`dotnet nuget push`, `mvn deploy`,
  `gradle publish`, `twine upload`/`pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish`, `docker push`/`docker/build-push-action`); release
  tools (`release-please`, `semantic-release`, GoReleaser, JReleaser); GitHub `environment:` with protection, Azure
  Pipelines `deployment` jobs with `environment:`, GitLab `environment:` + `when: manual`/protected environments.
- Fail: publish from a script meant for workstations (`publish.ps1` with a local API key); production deploy in the
  same job as the PR build; publish on every push with a constant version (also SV-03).

#### 8. Provenance and signing — SSDF-03, SSDF-12, SSDF-14, SLSA-03 … SLSA-07, OSC-18, OSC-19 (SL-05)

- Pass: `actions/attest-build-provenance`, `slsa-framework/slsa-github-generator` (L3 generator), `sigstore/cosign`
  (`cosign sign`/`attest`), `sigstore/gh-action-sigstore-python`, PyPI trusted publishing with attestations,
  `npm publish --provenance`, `dotnet nuget sign`, `maven-gpg-plugin`/Gradle `signing` plugin, `gpg --detach-sign`,
  published `SHA256SUMS`.
- Reproducible settings (SSDF-03): `<Deterministic>`/`<ContinuousIntegrationBuild>`, Maven
  `project.build.outputTimestamp`, `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`.
- Fail: provenance generated by a custom script using a producer key (SLSA-04).
- Note, don't fail here: signing key material read from a file committed to the repo (security finding, not
  lifecycle).

#### 9. Version fields and SemVer mapping — SV-01 … SV-11 (SL-03)

- .NET: `<Version>`, `<VersionPrefix>` + `<VersionSuffix>`, `Directory.Build.props`, `GitVersion.yml`/MinVer/
  Nerdbank (`version.json`).
- Java: Maven `<version>` (`-SNAPSHOT` = pre-release), Gradle `version =`.
- Python: `pyproject.toml` `[project] version` or dynamic (`setuptools_scm`). PEP 440: `1.4` → `1.4.0`;
  `1.0a1`/`b1`/`rc1`/`.dev1` = pre-release; `.post1` accepted.
- Not judged: `<AssemblyVersion>`/`<FileVersion>` 4-part values.
- Fail: `v1.2.3` in a manifest (SV-11), leading zeros (`1.02.0`), two-part non-PEP 440 versions (`1.2` in
  `.csproj`/`pom.xml`), the same fixed version published by every build (SV-03).

#### 10. Committed binaries — OSC-21 (SL-12)

- Fail patterns: `*.exe`, `*.dll`, `*.so`, `*.dylib`, `*.a`, `*.lib`, `*.o`, `*.obj`, `*.jar`, `*.war`, `*.ear`,
  `*.class`, `*.pyc`, `*.pyo`, `*.whl`, `*.nupkg`, `*.msi`.
- Exclude: paths matched by the target's `.gitignore`; `bin/`, `obj/`, `target/`, `build/`, `dist/`, `out/`,
  `__pycache__/`, `.venv/`, `node_modules/`; binaries referenced by a manifest (review-dependency-management DEP-08).
- Detection uses a name glob over the target, not the capped file list.
- `gradle-wrapper.jar` is common: report it, with a remark that wrapper validation
  (`gradle/actions/wrapper-validation`) mitigates it.

#### 11. SAST and gates — SSDF-04, SSDF-06 … SSDF-08, SSDF-16, OSC-14 (SL-11)

- Pass: `github/codeql-action` (`init` + `analyze`), Azure DevOps `AdvancedSecurity-Codeql-*` tasks, GitLab
  `SAST.gitlab-ci.yml` template, Semgrep (`semgrep ci`), SonarScanner with quality gate wait
  (`sonar.qualitygate.wait=true`), Security Code Scan / `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.NetAnalyzers` with
  `TreatWarningsAsErrors`, SpotBugs + FindSecBugs with `failOnError`, Bandit without `--exit-zero`; SARIF upload
  (`github/codeql-action/upload-sarif`).
- Fail: tool configured but only on `schedule`/manual; `continue-on-error: true` on the analysis step;
  `--exit-zero`/`ignoreFailures = true`; analyzers disabled (`<RunAnalyzers>false</RunAnalyzers>`).
- Lint/format rule content is not judged here (review-software-quality).

## File: `references/standards/semver.md`

*Load rule: SV-01…SV-11. Always load.*

### Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 — localized summary

- Level: the source's RFC 2119 keyword (MUST/SHOULD) or `REVIEW` (FAQ guidance), for information only; severity is the owning check's default.
- Version fields per ecosystem and their SemVer mapping: `../lifecycle-signals.md` §9 (SKILL.md version-ecosystem rule).

Every element belongs to **SL-03**.

| ID | Level | Requirement (summary) | Applies when | Check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SV-01 | MUST | The published version has the form X.Y.Z, non-negative integers without leading zeros (ecosystem mapping per `lifecycle-signals.md` §9). | a version is declared | SL-03 |
| SV-02 | MUST | A versioned library, package or API declares its public API (in code or docs), so that version bumps have a meaning. | publishes a library, package or versioned API | SL-03 |
| SV-03 | MUST | Released versions are immutable: changes ship as a new version. No re-publishing the same version, no constant version with publish-on-every-build. | publish step in scope | SL-03 |
| SV-04 | SHOULD | Software used in production or depended on by others is at 1.0.0 or later. 0.y.z signals unstable initial development. | 0.y.z version and a production deploy or public package | SL-03 |
| SV-05 | MUST | PATCH only for backward-compatible fixes, MINOR for backward-compatible additions **or new deprecations**, MAJOR for any incompatible API change. | change log or release notes label changes per version | SL-03 |
| SV-06 | MUST | Versions increase numerically (1.9.0 → 1.10.0), and lower components reset to 0 on a bump (1.4.2 → 1.5.0, not 1.5.2). | version history visible in a change log | SL-03 |
| SV-07 | MUST | Pre-release: hyphen + dot-separated identifiers of `[0-9A-Za-z-]`, none empty, numeric ones without leading zeros (ecosystem equivalents accepted). | a pre-release version is declared | SL-03 |
| SV-08 | MUST | Build metadata follows `+` with valid identifiers and is never the only difference between two releases. | build metadata in a version or version template | SL-03 |
| SV-09 | SHOULD | Functionality is deprecated (documented, released in a minor version) before it's removed in a major version. | change log shows removals | SL-03 |
| SV-10 | REVIEW | An accidental breaking change in a minor or patch release is fixed by a new release that restores compatibility, and is documented. Released versions are never modified. | change log mentions such a case | SL-03 |
| SV-11 | REVIEW | `v1.2.3` isn't a semantic version: a `v` prefix is fine in tag names, but the manifest version has no prefix. | manifest version or tag pattern in scope | SL-03 |

### NIST SP 800-218 SSDF Version 1.1 — localized summary

- Level: every element is `REVIEW` (the SSDF uses no normative keywords); severity is the owning check's default.

| ID | Level | Requirement (summary) | Applies when | Check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SSDF-01 | REVIEW | (PO.3.1, PO.3.2 ex. 3) The toolchain (build, test, analysis, release) is defined as code in the repository (pipelines-as-code), not only in a UI. | always | SL-01 |
| SSDF-02 | REVIEW | (PW.6.2 ex. 3, PO.5.1 ex. 4) Builds run in a dedicated, controlled build environment (the CI platform) with minimal direct human access, not ad hoc on workstations. | always | SL-01 |
| SSDF-03 | REVIEW | (PO.3.2 ex. 4) The technologies for reproducible builds are in place where the ecosystem supports them (deterministic compiler and packaging settings, fixed timestamps). | publishes artifacts | SL-05 |
| SSDF-04 | REVIEW | (PW.6.1, PW.6.2 ex. 1, 2, 7) Compiler and build-tool security and warning features are enabled in versioned build config, and warnings are treated as errors in CI builds. | compiled language in scope | SL-11 |
| SSDF-05 | REVIEW | (PO.3.2 ex. 5, 7) Toolchain components are kept updated, and their integrity and provenance are verified before use (pinned versions, checksum-verified downloads). | CI files in scope | SL-10 |
| SSDF-06 | REVIEW | (PO.4.1 ex. 3) Security-check criteria are defined (e.g. the severity threshold that blocks a merge, part of the definition of done). | security tooling in CI | SL-11 |
| SSDF-07 | REVIEW | (PO.4.2 ex. 1, 3) The toolchain gathers security-check results automatically and enforces the criteria as automated gates (the build fails on findings above the threshold). | security tooling in CI | SL-11 |
| SSDF-08 | REVIEW | (PO.3.3, PO.4.2 ex. 4) Security tools produce retained artifacts of their results (e.g. SARIF upload, reports) with restricted access. | security tooling in CI | SL-11 |
| SSDF-09 | REVIEW | (PO.5.1 ex. 2, 5) Environments are separated: production deployment runs as a distinct, protected stage or environment, and non-production pipelines don't use production resources. | deploy pipeline in scope | SL-02 |
| SSDF-10 | REVIEW | (PS.1.1 ex. 1, 4) Code and configuration-as-code follow least privilege, and the code owner reviews changes by others (CODEOWNERS or equivalent). | forge supports CODEOWNERS | SL-04 |
| SSDF-11 | REVIEW | (PS.1.1 ex. 3) Commit signing is required on protected branches. | settings-as-code in scope | SL-04 |
| SSDF-12 | REVIEW | (PS.1.1 ex. 5, 6; PS.2.1 ex. 1, 2) Release artifacts are code-signed and/or published with cryptographic hashes so acquirers can verify integrity. | publishes artifacts | SL-05 |
| SSDF-13 | REVIEW | (PS.3.1 ex. 1, 2) Release files and their integrity and provenance data are archived per release in a controlled repository (a registry or release store), not rebuilt on demand. | publishes artifacts | SL-02 |
| SSDF-14 | REVIEW | (PS.3.2 ex. 1, 3, 4) Provenance data is produced for every release in a standards-based format, is integrity-protected, and is updated whenever components change. | publishes artifacts | SL-05 |
| SSDF-15 | REVIEW | (PW.7.1, PW.7.2 ex. 1, 3) Peer code review is required for changes to protected branches. | settings-as-code in scope | SL-04 |
| SSDF-16 | REVIEW | (PW.7.2 ex. 4, 6) Automated static analysis checks code for vulnerabilities continuously as it's checked in, and findings are triaged. | always | SL-11 |
| SSDF-17 | REVIEW | (RV.1.1; RV.1.3 ex. 1) A vulnerability disclosure program is published, easy to find, and explains how to report. | always | SL-07 |
| SSDF-18 | REVIEW | (RV.1.3 ex. 2, 3) The policy states who handles reports and the response process (triage, remediation, communication). | security policy exists | SL-07 |
| SSDF-19 | REVIEW | (RV.2.2 ex. 3) Security advisories are released for fixed vulnerabilities, describing affected versions and how to remediate (supported versions are stated). | security policy exists | SL-07 |

## File: `references/standards/slsa.md`

*Load rule: SLSA-01…SLSA-14. Always load.*

### SLSA specification v1.2 — localized summary

- Level: the source's RFC 2119 keyword (MUST/SHOULD) for information only; severity is the owning check's default.
- Elements on Source-track settings (SLSA-10 … SLSA-14) are judged only from settings-as-code (SKILL.md settings-visibility rule).

| ID | Level | Requirement (summary) | Applies when | Check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SLSA-01 | MUST | Release artifacts are built on a hosted build platform able to reach the target Build level, not on a developer workstation. | publishes artifacts | SL-02 |
| SLSA-02 | MUST | The producer builds in a consistent way: one source-controlled build definition for every release, with ecosystem build metadata kept current. | always | SL-01 |
| SLSA-03 | MUST | The build generates provenance that identifies each output by digest and describes how it was built (SLSA Provenance format recommended). | publishes artifacts | SL-05 |
| SLSA-04 | MUST | Provenance is authentic: it's signed by the build platform's identity (e.g. keyless OIDC attestation), not by a key the build script controls. | provenance generated | SL-05 |
| SLSA-05 | MUST | (L3) Provenance is unforgeable and builds are isolated: provenance is generated in a trusted context that user build steps can't alter. | provenance generated | SL-05 |
| SLSA-06 | MUST | The producer distributes provenance to consumers with the artifact (registry attestation, release asset) or through the package ecosystem. | provenance generated | SL-05 |
| SLSA-07 | SHOULD | Attestations are tied to the specific release and artifact digests and are immutable once published. | provenance generated | SL-05 |
| SLSA-08 | MUST | The build platform follows security best practice: access control, frequent updates and prompt fixing of known vulnerabilities (secret management: see SMG-12). | CI files in scope | SL-10 |
| SLSA-09 | MUST | (Source L1) All source, including build and release configuration, is under version control. No build steps exist only outside the repository. | always | SL-01 |
| SLSA-10 | MUST | (Source L2) Access controls restrict sensitive operations, such as updating protected branches, to defined roles. | settings-as-code in scope | SL-04 |
| SLSA-11 | MUST | (Source L2) Protected branches only advance to descendant revisions: force-push is prohibited. | settings-as-code in scope | SL-04 |
| SLSA-12 | MUST | (Source L2) Release tags can't be moved or deleted (tag protection or immutable tags). | settings-as-code in scope | SL-04 |
| SLSA-13 | MUST | (Source L3) Claims such as "every change is tested before merge" are enforced by SCS technical controls (required status checks) and documented. | settings-as-code in scope | SL-04 |
| SLSA-14 | MUST | (Source L4) Two trusted persons agree to each change to a protected branch, including the final revision. | settings-as-code in scope | SL-04 |

## File: `references/standards/openssf-scorecard.md`

*Load rule: OSC-01…OSC-21. Always load.*

### OpenSSF Scorecard checks v5.6.0 — localized summary

- Level: every element is `REVIEW` (Scorecard describes heuristics, not normative requirements); severity is the owning check's default.
- Platform: Scorecard documents GitHub. For Azure Pipelines, GitLab CI and Jenkins apply the equivalents in `../lifecycle-signals.md`; if none exists, skip the element with "no equivalent on <platform>".

| ID | Level | Requirement (summary) | Applies when | Check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| OSC-01 | REVIEW | (Tier 1) Default and release branches block force pushes and deletion. | settings-as-code in scope | SL-04 |
| OSC-02 | REVIEW | (Tier 2) Changes need a pull request with ≥ 1 approval, also for administrators; the most recent push is approved; the branch is up to date before merging. | settings-as-code in scope | SL-04 |
| OSC-03 | REVIEW | (Tier 3) At least one status check must pass before merging. | settings-as-code in scope | SL-04 |
| OSC-04 | REVIEW | A CODEOWNERS file exists in a supported location and covers the repository or at least its sensitive paths (pipelines, build config). | forge supports CODEOWNERS | SL-04 |
| OSC-05 | REVIEW | (Tiers 4–5) Code-owner review or ≥ 2 reviewers are required, stale approvals are dismissed on new commits, and administrators are included. | settings-as-code in scope | SL-04 |
| OSC-06 | REVIEW | CI runs on pull/merge requests before merge, not only on push, schedule or manual triggers. | CI files in scope | SL-01 |
| OSC-07 | REVIEW | No `pull_request_target` or `workflow_run` workflow checks out and runs the PR's untrusted code (head ref/SHA). | GitHub workflows in scope | SL-09 |
| OSC-08 | REVIEW | Untrusted context values (issue/PR title and body, comment body, head ref, commit message) are never interpolated into inline scripts; pass them through environment variables instead. | CI files in scope | SL-09 |
| OSC-09 | REVIEW | Workflow tokens are least privilege: top-level `permissions` are read-only or empty, and write scopes are declared per job. | CI files in scope | SL-10 |
| OSC-10 | REVIEW | Sensitive write scopes (`actions`, `checks`, `contents`, `deployments`, `packages`, `security-events`, `statuses`) are granted only to jobs that need them, such as release/publish jobs. | CI files in scope | SL-10 |
| OSC-11 | REVIEW | Third-party actions, reusable workflows and pipeline tasks/templates are pinned to a full commit SHA, not a mutable tag or branch. | CI files in scope | SL-10 |
| OSC-12 | REVIEW | Container images used for building and releasing (Dockerfile `FROM`, job `container:`/`services:`) are pinned by digest. | CI Dockerfiles or job containers in scope | SL-10 |
| OSC-13 | REVIEW | Build and CI scripts don't pipe downloads into a shell, and CI installs use locked or hashed forms (`npm ci`, `pip --require-hashes`, `dotnet restore --locked-mode`). | CI/build scripts in scope | SL-10 |
| OSC-14 | REVIEW | A SAST tool (e.g. CodeQL, Semgrep, SonarQube/SonarCloud) runs on pull requests and/or pushes to the default branch. | always | SL-11 |
| OSC-15 | REVIEW | A security policy (`SECURITY.md`, case-insensitive) exists in the root, `.github/` or `docs/`. | always | SL-07 |
| OSC-16 | REVIEW | The policy gives a private reporting channel: an email address or an http(s) URL for reporting vulnerabilities. | security policy exists | SL-07 |
| OSC-17 | REVIEW | The policy has free text on the vulnerability process, disclosure expectations or timelines, beyond a bare link. | security policy exists | SL-07 |
| OSC-18 | REVIEW | The release workflow signs release artifacts (`.sig`, `.asc`, `.minisig`, `.sigstore`, `.sigstore.json`). | publishes artifacts | SL-05 |
| OSC-19 | REVIEW | The release workflow publishes SLSA provenance (`*.intoto.jsonl` or a registry attestation) with every release. | publishes artifacts | SL-05 |
| OSC-20 | REVIEW | Releases are published as a package or image through a packaging step in CI (registry push), so users get updates through a package manager. | publishes artifacts | SL-02 |
| OSC-21 | REVIEW | No generated executable artifacts (`.exe`, `.dll`, `.so`, `.dylib`, `.jar`, `.war`, `.class`, `.pyc`, …) are committed. Reviewable scripts, generated source and generated docs are allowed. | always (committed-binary rule) | SL-12 |

### Azure Well-Architected Framework — safe deployment practices — localized summary

| ID | Level | Requirement (summary) | Applies when | Check |
